newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-CORINTHIANS COACH WALKS OUT ON CLUB.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CORINTHIANS COACH WALKS OUT ON CLUB.

text.p: Coach Nelsinho quit Sao Paulo's Corinthians on Friday, becoming the third Brazilian first division coach to resign this week and the sixth since the national championship kicked off in July.
Nelsinho's walkout was thought to be caused by a row with club directors. "I decided to leave because I've lost the happiness of working here," he said.
"I like it here... but there's no more motivation to work here."
He was reportedly angry over a proposal to sell left-back Andre Luis to Spanish club Tenerife.
Corinthians, who spent $20 million on new signings this year, won the Paulista championship in the first half of the season, but currently lie sixth in the national championship.
Elsewhere, Cruzeiro coach Paulo Autuori left his club on Thursday, one day after his side won the South American Libertadores Cup. He immediately joined Rio de Janeiro's Flamengo.
News of the move leaked out the week before and there was criticism at Flamengo over the way coach Sebastiao Rocha, who made way for Autuori, had been treated.
Rocha departed with a 4-2 win away to Atletico Mineiro on Tuesday and said: "With a young team like this it is normal to have ups and downs." Flamengo are currently seven places off the bottom.
Fluminense, Gremio and Goias have also changed coaches.
Bottom side Fluminense, relegated last year but reinstated by the Brazilian Football Confederation on the eve of the championship, dismissed Hugo de Leon after just two matches.
